items.articleBody:
[Die Yoto-Player](https://eu.yotoplay.com) gehören für uns zu den interessantesten Audioplayern für Kinder. Wir nutzen privat sowohl den kleinen Mini als auch den größeren Yoto Player und schätzen an beiden Geräten vor allem die Offenheit des Systems. Anders als bei vielen konkurrierenden Angeboten beschränkt sich Yoto nicht auf einen Katalog kostenpflichtiger Inhalte.

#### Der neue Yoto Mini der 4. Generation

Auch eigene MP3-Dateien, Podcasts und Internetradiosender lassen sich einbinden. Wer die Sendung mit der Maus, Anna und die wilden Tiere oder andere Kinderpodcasts hören möchte, kann diese ebenso nutzen wie reine Kindermusiksender, eigene Sprachaufnahmen oder selbst gerippte CDs.

Damit können die Geräte weit mehr, als ihre zunächst recht einfache Bedienung vermuten lässt. Im Familienalltag hat sich dieses Konzept bewährt. Die Kinder können ihre Inhalte selbst auswählen, während Eltern die Übersicht behalten und nicht für jeden neuen Hörinhalt zusätzliches Geld ausgeben müssen. Wir haben uns in den vergangenen Jahren viele Kinder-Audioplayer angesehen und sogar eigene Musikboxen gebaut. Letztlich sind wir bei Yoto geblieben, weil das System für uns die fairsten Nutzungsgrenzen mit einer der einfachsten Bedienoberflächen verbindet.

#### Yoto Mini 4 liefert Musik und Hörspiele

Mit dem [Yoto Mini der vierten Generation](https://eu.yotoplay.com/players/yoto-mini-4) hat der Hersteller sein kompaktes Modell nun überarbeitet. Die neue Ausgabe [kostet in Deutschland 99,99 Euro](https://www.ifun.de/amzn/B0HHNJF5XV) und bringt neben mehr Speicher und aktueller Funktechnik auch eine wichtige Veränderung bei der Bedienung mit. Über einen zusätzlichen grünen Dreh- und Druckknopf lassen sich erstmals mehrere Lieblingsinhalte direkt am Gerät auswählen, ohne dass dafür eine Karte benötigt wird. Gleichzeitig bietet der Mini ein höher aufgelöstes Display und ist besser gegen Wasser und Staub geschützt. Das sind keine grundsätzlichen Veränderungen des bisherigen Konzepts, sondern Verbesserungen, die uns im Alltag durchaus gefallen.

## Hörspielkarten bleiben Teil des Konzepts

Yoto setzt [auch bei der neuen Generation](https://www.ifun.de/yoto-player-4-und-mini-4-neue-generation-mit-schnellzugriff-288703/) auf physische Karten, mit denen Kinder ihre gewünschten Inhalte starten können. Eine Karte wird in den Player gesteckt und ruft das zugehörige Hörspiel oder andere Audioinhalte auf. Diese Form der Bedienung ist bewusst einfach gehalten und kommt ohne Smartphone aus. Die Karten machen die verfügbaren Inhalte zudem greifbar. Kinder können ihre Sammlung durchsehen, eine Geschichte auswählen und selbstständig starten. Für die jüngeren Nutzer ist das ein nachvollziehbares Konzept, das sich deutlich von der Bedienung gewöhnlicher Bluetooth-Lautsprecher unterscheidet.

#### Unsere Sammlung besteht inzwischen aus über 50 Karten

Besonders gut gefällt uns seit jeher, dass Yoto nicht auf den eigenen Kartenkatalog beschränkt ist. Mit den [sogenannten „Make Your Own“-Cards](https://www.ifun.de/amzn/B09N7W47CL) lassen sich eigene Inhalte hinterlegen. Dazu gehören beispielsweise Hörspiele aus der persönlichen MP3-Sammlung, selbst zusammengestellte Wiedergabelisten oder andere Audiodateien. Auch Podcasts und Internetradio spielen im Yoto-System eine wichtige Rolle. Die Inhalte werden über die zugehörige App und eine Weboberfläche verwaltet. Auf diese Weise lässt sich der Player an die Vorlieben der Kinder anpassen, ohne vollständig von den Veröffentlichungen und Preisen eines einzelnen Anbieters abhängig zu sein.

Wir nutzen beispielsweise keine fertig bespielten Hörspielkarten, sondern kaufen ausschließlich die leeren Karten, die wir anschließend selbst mit unseren Inhalten verknüpfen. Neue Hörspiele kommen aus der eigenen Sammlung, werden gekauft, aus der Bücherei ausgeliehen oder im Freundeskreis weitergegeben.

#### Die bunte Bibliothek setzt auf selbst zusammengestellte Inhalte

CDs lassen sich in die persönliche Musikbibliothek übernehmen, die dann auch auf dem Rechner, über Sonos-Lautsprecher oder später auf dem eigenen Smartphone verwendet werden kann. Yoto ist für uns lediglich eine zusätzliche Möglichkeit, diese Sammlung in den frühen Kinderjahren zugänglich zu machen. Das ist aus unserer Sicht deutlich nachhaltiger, als sämtliche Hörspiele ausschließlich innerhalb eines geschlossenen Systems zu sammeln.

## Eigene MP3s und faire Nutzungsgrenzen

Die Verwaltung der eigenen Inhalte ist unkompliziert. Über die Weboberfläche von Yoto laden wir unsere MP3-Dateien hoch, erstellen Wiedergabelisten, sortieren einzelne Titel und stellen unterschiedliche Sammlungen zusammen. Anschließend lässt sich eine Playlist mit einer Make Your Own Card verknüpfen. Besonders angenehm ist, dass diese Zuordnung direkt über die iPhone-App funktioniert. Dazu halten wir die Karte kurz an die Rückseite des iPhones und legen fest, welche Wiedergabeliste sie künftig aufrufen soll. Sobald das Kind die Karte in seinen Yoto Player steckt, startet die entsprechende Zusammenstellung.

Für die „Make Your Own“-Cards, die im Zehnerpack rund 25 Euro kosten, gelten ausgesprochen faire Grenzen: Pro selbst erstellter Karten-Playlist können bis zu 100 Titel mit insgesamt höchstens 500 MB beziehungsweise fünf Stunden Audio hinterlegt werden. Ein einzelner Track darf maximal 100 MB groß beziehungsweise eine Stunde lang sein. Zum Vergleich: Die sogenannten Kreativ-Tonies, die auf der Toniebox eine vergleichbare Funktion erfüllen, bieten lediglich 90 Minuten für eigene Hörinhalte und kosten einzeln 13 Euro. Wer regelmäßig neue Inhalte zusammenstellt, merkt diesen Unterschied schnell.

#### Die Cleo Fischer Geschichten stammen aus der ARD Audiothek

Yoto erlaubt zudem, eigene Grafiken für Wiedergabelisten und einzelne Titel zu hinterlegen. Diese werden auf dem kleinen Display des Players angezeigt, wenn eine Karte eingelegt oder ein bestimmtes Kapitel abgespielt wird. Damit lassen sich auch selbst zusammengestellte Hörspiele visuell ansprechend aufbereiten. Die Grafiken helfen Kindern, ihre Inhalte wiederzuerkennen, ohne dass sie bereits lesen können müssen. Wir schätzen diese Möglichkeit, weil sich damit auch die eigene Hörspielbibliothek ähnlich komfortabel bedienen lässt wie offiziell angebotene Karten.

## Grüner Knopf für häufig genutzte Inhalte

Die auffälligste Neuerung der vierten Generation ist ein grüner Dreh- und Druckknopf auf der Vorderseite. Er ergänzt die bisherige Kartenbedienung um einen direkten Zugriff auf häufig gehörte Inhalte. Eltern können dafür in der Yoto-App zwei Sammlungen von Wiedergabelisten zusammenstellen, eine für den Tag und eine für die Nacht. Jede dieser Sammlungen darf bis zu 20 Einträge enthalten. Die Auswahl kann jederzeit über die App verändert werden. So lassen sich neue Lieblingsgeschichten hinzufügen und ältere Inhalte wieder entfernen, ohne dass dafür eine zusätzliche Karte benötigt wird.

#### Der Grüne Knopf lässt sich mit eigenen Wiedergabelisten belegen

Die Bedienung ist ausgesprochen einfach. Ein Druck auf den grünen Knopf öffnet die Favoritenauswahl auf dem ebenfalls überarbeiteten, höher aufgelösten Display. Durch Drehen des Knopfs blättert man anschließend durch die hinterlegten Inhalte und ihre zugehörigen Grafiken. Hat man die gewünschte Geschichte gefunden, wird diese direkt gestartet. Für Kinder, die bereits mit dem Yoto Player vertraut sind, ist das schnell verstanden. Bei uns war die Gewöhnung an die neue Taste nach ungefähr zwei Minuten abgeschlossen.

Besonders interessant ist die Offenheit dieser Favoritenfunktion. Die Listen sind nicht auf gekaufte Yoto-Karten begrenzt. Auch eigene Make-Your-Own-Zusammenstellungen, Podcasts und Radiosender können verwendet werden. Ebenso lassen sich bereits in der Yoto-Bibliothek vorhandene Inhalte auswählen. Damit wird der grüne Knopf zu einer zweiten Möglichkeit, den Player zu bedienen. Die klassische Karte bleibt für einzelne Hörspiele und Geschichten erhalten, häufig genutzte Angebote können daneben unmittelbar am Gerät bereitstehen.

#### Yoto mini: Der neue, grüne Knopf in Aktion

## Lieblingshörspiele auch ohne Karte

Gerade mit Kindern kennt man die Situation, dass die gerade gewünschte Hörspielkarte nicht dort liegt, wo sie eigentlich sein sollte. Mal befindet sie sich in einer anderen Tasche, mal im Kinderzimmer und manchmal ist sie schlicht nicht aufzufinden. Hier bietet die neue Funktion einen echten Vorteil. Der Mini kann auf Reisen mitgenommen werden, ohne dass zusätzlich eine Auswahl physischer Karten eingepackt werden muss. Bis zu 20 Lieblingsinhalte stehen in jeder der beiden Sammlungen direkt über den grünen Knopf zur Verfügung.

#### Yoto mini im Regelbetrieb: Karte rein und loshören

Die getrennten Listen für Tag und Nacht erlauben es außerdem, unterschiedliche Inhalte bereitzustellen. Tagsüber könnten beispielsweise Musik, Podcasts oder längere Hörspiele angeboten werden, während abends ruhigere Geschichten zur Auswahl stehen. Für uns ist dabei weniger die konkrete Trennung der Tageszeiten entscheidend als die Möglichkeit, den Player ohne zusätzliche Karten mit einer sinnvollen Auswahl an Inhalten auszustatten. Das macht ihn vor allem für Kinder interessant, die ihre Lieblingsgeschichten bereits kennen und gezielt auswählen möchten.

Der grüne Knopf verändert damit auch ein Stück weit die Rolle der Hörspielkarten. Diese bleiben eine schöne Möglichkeit, neue Inhalte zu verschenken, Sammlungen anzulegen oder den jüngeren Kindern eine unmittelbar verständliche Bedienung zu bieten. Mit zunehmendem Alter dürfte die direkte Auswahl am Gerät aber immer wichtiger werden. Der Yoto Mini wächst dadurch besser mit seinen Nutzern mit, ohne dass das bisherige Bedienkonzept aufgegeben werden muss.

## 64 GB Speicher für Offline-Inhalte

Ein weiterer Fortschritt betrifft den internen Speicher. Sowohl der neue Yoto Mini als auch der größere Player verfügen jetzt über 64 GB. Eine Kapazität, die laut Hersteller für mehr als 1.000 Stunden Audiomaterial reicht, das anschließend auch ohne aktive Internetverbindung abgespielt werden kann. Besonders bei einem für Kinder gedachten Audioplayer halten wir ausreichend Offline-Speicher für wichtig. Im Auto, auf Reisen oder unterwegs steht schließlich nicht immer eine WLAN-Verbindung zur Verfügung. Ein Player, auf dem bereits eine größere Auswahl an Geschichten gespeichert ist, lässt sich entsprechend unabhängiger einsetzen.

#### Wilder Mix aus Lerninhalten, gerippten Kauf-CDs, Podcasts und Internet-Hits

Sehr gut gefällt uns, wie Yoto die Offline-Verfügbarkeit organisiert. Die auf dem eigenen Konto hinterlegten Inhalte werden automatisch auf den Player geladen, wenn dieser mit dem WLAN verbunden ist und am Strom hängt. Wir müssen uns deshalb nicht vor jeder Reise darum kümmern, welche Hörspiele noch schnell übertragen werden sollen. Stattdessen befinden sich die regelmäßig genutzten Inhalte bereits auf dem Gerät. Ob die gewünschten Dateien vollständig heruntergeladen wurden, lässt sich zudem in der iPhone-App kontrollieren. Gerade vor längeren Autofahrten oder einem Urlaub ohne zuverlässiges WLAN ist das hilfreich.

#### In die Yoto-Cloud geladen werden die Inhalte über eine Web-Oberfläche

Dabei sollte man den internen Speicher nicht mit dem persönlichen Cloud-Speicher für selbst erstellte Karten verwechseln. Die 64 GB befinden sich direkt auf dem Yoto Mini und dienen der lokalen Wiedergabe. Die Grenzen von 100 Titeln und 500 MB für eine eigene Karten-Playlist bleiben davon unberührt. Es ist also nicht notwendig, zusätzliche Make Your Own Cards zu besitzen, um den internen Speicher vollständig nutzen zu können. Umgekehrt erhöht ein großer interner Speicher nicht automatisch die Kapazität einer einzelnen selbst erstellten Playlist. Yoto hat uns diese Trennung auf Nachfrage ausdrücklich bestätigt. Für Familien, die viele eigene Audiodateien einbinden möchten, ist das eine wichtige und gute Information.

## Robuster und weiterhin kompakt

Ebenfalls erneuert wurde die Funktechnik. Der Yoto Mini 4 unterstützt Wi-Fi 6 und Bluetooth 6.1. Damit ist die technische Grundlage für die Verbindung zum Heimnetz und zu Bluetooth-Zubehör aktualisiert worden. Ob daraus im Alltag spürbare Vorteile gegenüber der Vorgängergeneration entstehen, hängt allerdings von der jeweiligen Nutzung ab. Wir haben keine großen Leistungssprünge wahrgenommen. Beim gewöhnlichen Abspielen eines Hörspiels sind die Anforderungen an die Datenübertragung ohnehin gering.

#### Yoto und Yoto mini: Links die 3. rechts die 4. Generation

Auch bei der Hardware hat Yoto nachgebessert. Der neue Mini ist nach IP67 gegen das Eindringen von Staub und Wasser geschützt. Gerade für ein Gerät, das Kinder regelmäßig selbst in die Hand nehmen und überallhin mitnehmen, ist das eine sinnvolle Verbesserung. Im Unterschied zu einem stationären Audioplayer landet der Mini schließlich auch im Rucksack, im Auto oder unterwegs neben anderen Spielsachen. Das Gewicht gibt Yoto mit 185 Gramm an. Damit bleibt der Mini ein vergleichsweise handliches Gerät, das Kinder gut transportieren können.

An der grundsätzlichen Ausrichtung hat sich nichts geändert: Der kleine Player funktioniert bei heruntergeladenen Inhalten unabhängig von einer Internetverbindung und lässt sich ohne komplizierte Menüs bedienen. Im Unterschied zu einem gewöhnlichen Bluetooth-Lautsprecher müssen Kinder nicht darauf warten, dass ein Erwachsener die gewünschte Wiedergabe am Telefon startet. Stattdessen greifen sie zur passenden Karte oder zum grünen Favoritenknopf. Diese Selbstständigkeit gehört für uns zu den größten Vorteilen des gesamten Yoto-Konzepts.

## Kopfhöreranschluss und zwölf Stunden Akku

Erfreulich ist außerdem, dass Yoto den klassischen Kopfhöreranschluss beibehält. Kinder können damit weiterhin kabelgebundene Kopfhörer verwenden. Zusätzlich lassen sich Bluetooth-Kopfhörer verbinden. Gerade auf Reisen ist diese Wahlmöglichkeit praktisch. Die Akkulaufzeit gibt Yoto beim Mini mit bis zu zwölf Stunden an. Geladen wird per USB-C. Insgesamt bleibt der kompakte Player damit ein Gerät, das sich ebenso gut für die Hörspielstunde im Kinderzimmer wie für längere Autofahrten oder den Urlaub eignet.

#### Gummihülle und Schlaufe sollte man sich auf jeden Fall zulegen

Wer sich für das Yoto-System interessiert, hat weiterhin die Wahl zwischen dem kompakten Mini und dem größeren Player. Beide Geräte der vierten Generation erhalten den neuen grünen Knopf, 64 GB Speicher und die aktualisierte Funktechnik. Der große Yoto Player 4 kostet 129,99 Euro und bringt zusätzliche Eigenschaften für den stationären Einsatz mit. Dazu gehören ein überarbeitetes Nachtlicht mit sieben Farben, drahtloses Laden und eine vom Hersteller angegebene Akkulaufzeit von bis zu 14 Stunden. Außerdem soll sich dessen Akku austauschen lassen. Ein entsprechendes Ersatzset wurde für 2027 angekündigt.

Der Mini richtet sich dagegen weiterhin stärker an Familien, die ihren Audioplayer regelmäßig mitnehmen möchten. Seine kompakten Abmessungen, das geringe Gewicht und der zusätzliche Schutz gegen Wasser und Staub passen gut zu diesem Einsatzbereich. Das größere Modell ist mit seinem Nachtlicht und den zusätzlichen Lademöglichkeiten eher für einen festen Platz im Kinderzimmer gedacht. Wir würden diese Unterschiede nicht als grundsätzliche Vor- oder Nachteile bewerten. Entscheidend ist, wo das Gerät hauptsächlich verwendet werden soll.

## Die Software bleibt das wichtigste Argument

Aus unserer langjährigen Nutzung verschiedener Kinder-Audioplayer wissen wir, dass die Qualität eines solchen Geräts nicht allein von seiner Hardware abhängt. Entscheidend ist vielmehr, wie unkompliziert sich Inhalte verwalten und den Kindern zugänglich machen lassen. Hier hat Yoto mit seinen wiederbeschreibbaren Karten, der Weboberfläche und der Unterstützung eigener Audiodateien eine sehr gute Grundlage geschaffen. Die neue Favoritenfunktion baut diese Stärke weiter aus. Schön ist, dass der grüne Knopf auf Wunsch auch ausschließlich eigene Inhalte, ausgewählte Podcasts, Radiosender und selbst erstellte Zusammenstellungen zur Verfügung stellt. Hier werben keine kostenpflichtigen Inhalte um Aufmerksamkeit, und der Anbieter versucht nicht, die Kinder bei jeder Gelegenheit zum Kauf weiterer Hörspiele zu bewegen.

#### Die eigene Yoto-Sammlung lässt sich auch auf dem iPhone wiedergeben

Besonders wichtig ist uns dabei, dass die eigene Hörspielbibliothek auch außerhalb des Yoto-Systems erhalten bleibt. Wer seine MP3-Sammlung selbst pflegt, kann dieselben Geschichten später auf anderen Geräten verwenden. Das betrifft den heimischen Computer ebenso wie vorhandene Sonos-Lautsprecher oder irgendwann das eigene Smartphone der Kinder. Yoto bietet für diese Inhalte eine besonders kindgerechte Oberfläche, ohne dass man die eigene Sammlung dafür aufgeben müsste. Genau diese Kombination aus eigenständiger Bedienung und vergleichsweise offenen Nutzungsmöglichkeiten hat uns schon bei den früheren Generationen überzeugt.

Unterm Strich ist die [vierte Generation des Yoto Mini](https://www.ifun.de/amzn/B0HHNJF5XV) eine nachvollziehbare Weiterentwicklung, die noch besser mit älter werdenden Kindern mitwächst. Mehr Offline-Speicher, ein höher aufgelöstes Display und die zusätzliche Möglichkeit zum direkten Starten von Lieblingsinhalten passen gut zu den Anforderungen, die wir aus der bisherigen Nutzung kennen. Die größte Neuerung ist für uns nicht Wi-Fi 6 oder Bluetooth 6.1, sondern der unkomplizierte Zugriff auf digitale Favoriten. Kinder können ihre Inhalte selbstständig auswählen, und Eltern bleiben bei der Zusammenstellung der Hörspielbibliothek flexibel. Für uns ist Yoto deshalb weiterhin das überzeugendste Konzept für junge Kinder und Eltern, die deren Audioinhalte gerne selbst zusammenstellen.

items.articleBody:
Before we rush to pass honest judgments on the actions taken by Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska (analyzed in detail [↗ verfassungsblog.de](https://verfassungsblog.de/whose-coup-polish-constitutional-tribunal-crisis/) and here) aimed at saving whatever still remains of the authority of the Constitution ([the Constitutional Court as we used to know it ceased to exist long ago](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/israel-law-review/article/when-legal-fundamentalism-meets-political-justice-the-case-of-poland/99F9CFE7FE8196B568D4A1464D811890)), we need to be honest about the starting point of our discussion and embrace its broader constitutional context. While the critique they offer along the lines of correct-incorrect dichotomy might be appropriate for our good faith disagreements in normal times, it is plainly insufficient in extraordinary times we find ourselves in today. When two of your top courts have been captured and staffed with the usurpers that have been poisoning with total impunity the legal system for years now, one must change course substantially and think out of the conceptual fitted-for-good-times toolbox.

Judge Korwin-Piotrowska have suspended an individual who was never truly the President of the Constitutional Tribunal and has blatantly usurped this public function ([a crime under Polish law](https://sip.lex.pl/akty-prawne/dzu-dziennik-ustaw/kodeks-karny-16798683/art-227)). In my view: she had to. In November 2026, we reached a critical juncture where there has been no other option left – and very soon, there will be no time left at all. And yet, many – devoted only to legal texts and formalities – have embarked on yet another round of legal disputes, a futile, ritualistic kabuki dance around the paragraphs. They continue fiddle while Rome had been already burnt and they never came up with anything else than a litany of reasons why nothing could have been done since early 2024 without allegedly infringing the legality. I find it infuriating, as it exposes their in-built unwillingness to critically rethink what is legally and factually possible in these extraordinary times: to adapt, revisit and contextualize their recipes for [rebuilding the rule of law](https://verfassungsblog.de/hostile-constitutional-interpretation/). As Judge Korwin-Piotrowska has demonstrated, we must chart our course with fidelity to the Constitution and its values and finally make them integral part of the constitutional, not merely statutory, legality.

## Understanding the Context and Game of Appearances

Between 2015 and 2023, [the constitutional profile of the Polish state has been altered](https://www.zeit.de/politik/ausland/2021-08/tomasz-tadeusz-koncewicz-verfassungsrechtler-polen-eu-rechtsstaatprinzip). We did not have a mere crisis of the rule of law but rather a ruthless [war against the Constitution](https://kulturaliberalna.pl/2021/03/02/trwa-wojna-przeciw-konstytucji/). This occurred with unconstitutional resolutions of the Sejm, unconstitutionally hostile “rulings” issued by the usurpers masquerading as constitutional judges and, most often, by *de facto* actions based on sheer and blunt unconstrained force. Together, they turned out to be lethal to the institutions (as it turned out, extremely fragile and weak) and the culture of the rule of law on the ground. Therefore, when we talk about the rebuild, our restorative measures must not be merely technical and normative in nature. Rather, any solution adopted must pursue the primary goal of restoring meaning to the key elements of our legal and civic vocabulary. This vocabulary was stripped of any relevance and manipulated in the service of the ruthless majoritarian politics behind the [constitutional capture](https://www.eurozine.com/rising-to-the-challenge-of-constitutional-capture/).

We have now seen (again) the tragic consequences of living side by side with constitutional lawlessness. On 30 October 2026, in front of what used to be the Constitutional Court in Warsaw, we realised how much the constitutional profile of the state had been distorted.

With the starting point clearly identified, we must then look at the process of restoring the rule of law from [a situational perspective](https://verfassungsblog.de/militant-rule-of-law/). Given the scale of unconstitutional destruction in the 2015- 2023, the rebuilding must be about *optimal* and *always perfectible* *,* rather than, perfect solutions. Hence, we must embrace what is possible from a legal and factual perspective within the framework set out by the Constitution, its principles and values, and the binding judgments of supranational and international courts. Optimal and never perfect is at the heart of my argument. For the choice of strategies and methods must be always determined by the distribution of constitutional values in each case, the consequences of maintaining a situation inconsistent with the constitutional document for the entire legal order, and, last but not least, by keeping fresh the memories of the unprecedented ruthlessness with which the system was destroyed *per fas et nefas*. These emotions and memories have nothing to do with revanchism, which I reject, but rather should be considered as part of the good-faith calculation of how to act and what solutions to choose to restore the Constitution to its rightful place as the highest law of the land. It must be clear that those who leave with bad faith and arrogance in their hearts and a clear “track record” of the destruction of the rule of law cannot continue to have an advantage over those who want to restore the integrity of the Constitution. Unfortunately, they continue to enjoy it since we have accepted with legalistic helplessness the many booby traps and poison, they have left behind them. Their impudence has been on full display on 30 October 2026.

Finally *,* our methods must be proportionate to the extent of the lawlessness on the ground and the consequences of maintaining the illegal *status quo*. Our legal imagination might fuel change, but only when followed by a willingness to act and counteract outside the box. Thinking outside the box is only possible if we have the courage to critically reevaluate our existing language and tools. Restoring the rule of law is a process that will be a combination of actions of different nature and intensity. Some of them will be the realization of legalism, understood as compliance with the letter of the law, and some will require something more to protect constitutional values.

All this does not mean, however, which is crucial for proper understanding of the actions of Judge Korwin-Piotrowska, that what goes beyond the textual letter of the law must be automatically categorized as unlawful (which is the empty mantra that drives the actions and arguments of formalist and literalist lawyers) just as not every interpretation that goes beyond the wording of a legal provision must be unlawful in a situation where our literal interpretation would lead to an absurd or obviously unjust result(s). Just as we accept that we can overcome a linguistic interpretation to exclude absurdity or injustice, the same must go for the choice of methods to restore the rule of law. Sometimes relying only on the letter of the law will lead to absurd and self-destructive consequences, although in the name of formal legalism. For example, it is naïve to wait until the compromised judges of the fake constitutional court are gone or believe that they will convert and suddenly become loyal servants of the constitutional document.

This naivety was again on full display on 30 October 2026 in front of the old and gone Constitutional Court and later painfully corroborated by how stubborn and happy-go-lucky lawyers responded.

## Polish Trojan Horse

Following dramatic [events that unfolded both outside and inside](https://www.economist.com/europe/2026/11/01/will-polands-war-over-the-rule-of-law-ever-end) the building on Szucha Street in Warsaw, [Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a televised address](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jPH7_WJ0VQM), finally spoke of the necessity for the state to defend itself against those who undermine its constitutional order and principles. In essence, this statement alluded to the concept of “[militant democracy](https://academic.oup.com/icon/article/4/3/586/646375?login=false)” – an approach aimed at protecting a democratic system from enemies who attack it from within by exploiting democratic tools.

In Poland, it was always easy to discern which actors on the political stage remained within the bounds of acceptable criticism of the state and its institutions and thus deserved to enjoy the privileges afforded by a democratic system. There is no doubt that Law and Justice (PiS) has always been a classic example of a [disloyal opposition](https://press.jhu.edu/books/title/8634/breakdown-democratic-regimes). The party was built upon a consistent rejection of the legal system in force in Poland, as well as the 1997 Constitution – a document it never accepted as its own. Consequently, by definition, it positioned itself in opposition to the values and principles enshrined in that Constitution. Its politicians spoke contemptuously of the changes that followed 1989, dismissing them as the result of a [“rotten compromise” reached at the 1989 Round Table](https://watermark02.silverchair.com/moz043.pdf?token=AQECAHi208BE49Ooan9kkhW_Ercy7Dm3ZL_9Cf3qfKAc485ysgAAAmAwggJcBgkqhkiG9w0BBwagggJNMIICSQIBADCCAkIGCSqGSIb3DQEHATAeBglghkgBZQMEAS4wEQQMh1VJZR8_xVBcfNfeAgEQgIICE62-jllO2flx2tyBAiUaWrgEsvdqaSa9LlrZFQS-hrrvZs6Ys_MczHP3PhTfCf8BPFP1rMJHmdGAyg32R9yjOHn1J-lPR8CD_p9UAh61SVXaiiajQqQ9pp80qG_n16V0GlmUQwhS9gHfoiUkBjrdikodHmoGmLODlaRQIzdJTJLT4U2f57xSr9pjBlAMkN1gRchX6E6T4BpQQCRC10f4Vc4rBZKAuaX1Re0FiD19S43UBs7EJmyiQrBy71NZK40qgUHSuwvTT4EPuFjii-eaUUIfIwxSHyy9J35TVBrSUmmSkVFNOJy-7LFl97oQE7Soi1WLf8dciO3yx1RSWwsHep4ghggYsC-GT5BZXLSbSimN0YPgll490aVKPC0VWgrwM5DP6c2Hlnmd2XeidwBIdept_kr5dn4d0Ps2YORQy7a9_ZiEwT7hlPhIW3RLswtQ299imeAiIISSz1otWhbnVth1pF20miscpJx7E8woxaamzdiMr5ci4dAvkahrhWGxML2fFnu9GFstq9XWf1f8myMlsEoLV_FypCUPrDX41GJvuDD7ao58DCa3C-6xczjfKEEUslfSKeOjEYx4--8iBKWUYBLVxITl_D3GLyElGW4vmnXmSrFuRpIKBsumHn-tmffA-W8YTbJT0J6s-rk4YTbMCfmczsb5EbHQ_zqLVD6xkOmZ_LYAwEtl8SXFVqzzYek_pA). While the success of Poland’s peaceful political transition served as a model for others, for PiS, it represented an act of capitulation to foreign interests – specifically Western ones, and above all, German ones. To them, the democratic republic of Poland was an alien entity – a mere phantasm – that had to be destroyed, along with its institutions, to make way for something new and “better”. PiS tolerated fascist-leaning militant groups, sowed hatred, and encouraged aggressive behavior during the so-called “Independence Marches”. It excluded people from the national community, stigmatized them, and fueled antagonism. Terms such as “we shall reclaim”, “we shall conquer” and “we shall end this period of enslavement” were introduced into the language of public discourse. Antagonism, hatred, and a lack of acceptance for others – simply because they are “different” – became the hallmarks of a narrative that dominated the years 2015-2023, a dark period for [the rule of law](https://verfassungsblog.de/poland-and-europe-at-a-critical-juncture-what-has-happened-what-is-happening-whats-next/). This went well beyond the kind of criticism of a political opponent that is acceptable in any democratic system – a system that permits, and even embraces, political dispute, provided it remains within the bounds of the law and the constitutional order. Instead, the objective was the rejection and delegitimization of an “enemy” deemed to have no right to even exist, let alone compete for a democratic mandate.

And yet, despite all these warning signs, the democratic system in place in Poland looked the other way, effectively accepting a Trojan horse that grazed in the pastures of the Polish Republic’s liberal democracy, all the while despising that very system and viewing it as a mortal enemy. Thus, when PiS has finally seized power, it carried out an unconstitutional *coup d’état* which has been predicated on the long-standing and well-known political agenda. Once this “horse” was finally allowed into the city, it has done exactly what it had set out to do: it has fundamentally altered the city’s constitutional profile. To this day, no one has been held accountable for it.

On 30 October 2026, however, the Trojan horse powerfully reared its ugly head on Szucha Street in a manner as chilling as it was ominous.

## Why Not Earlier?

Why were preemptive defensive measures not taken sooner? And why, after 2023, discussion regarding the rebuild of the rule of law did not unfold hand in hand with the equally fundamental question of how to protect democracy and the rule of law? A pernicious logic always prevailed: political calculation took (and takes) precedence over fidelity to the Constitution. And yet, a well-governed and well-organized state should be capable of identifying threats and holding those responsible to account – all within the framework of the existing legal system, and by utilizing the institutions and procedures of the rule of law. By the time liberal Poland finally begins to grasp its obligation to take defensive action, it may unfortunately be too late – and the current approach creates the impression that it is acting blindly, lacking a coherent plan.

In November 2026, these lessons not learnt and missed opportunities came back to haunt us. The counterattack launched by an unconstitutional body – backed by usurpers within other co-opted institutions (the so-called Supreme Court and its fake President) – must serve as definitive proof that the time for deliberation and splitting hairs has long passed. We have endured not only eight long years of the dismantling of the rule of law, but also three additional years following the elections of October 2023 of endless and fruitless discussions. There was ample time to determine the necessary steps to restore the respect for the Constitution and basic decency in public life. Three long years of procrastinations only fortified the usurpers in their impunity. If today we continue to delay a systemic halt to the unlawful operations of the usurpers, they will persist in poisoning the legal system. They will exploit the authority of a court – an authority never rightfully theirs – to shield themselves and grow ever more emboldened. This is painful for any decent citizen who still believes in the rule of law. For me personally, it is a source of deep frustration and regret that three years have not been enough for every reasonable democrat to grasp who the true enemy of Polish democracy is and plan his actions accordingly.

## Embrace the Constitution or Perish

The “constitutional fidelity” (see also [↗ e-elgar.com](https://www.e-elgar.com/shop/gbp/sustaining-the-rule-of-law-9781035345465.html) ) serves as the ultimate guide for a properly understood legalism – one rooted in constitutional values rather than just the narrow, literalistic adherence to individual taken-out-of-context paragraphs so beloved in Poland. It invites us to make the Constitution and its values integral part of our understanding of constitutional legality. It was precisely this kind of fidelity and animus that guided Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska. Acting in good faith and with integrity, she finally provided a much-needed counternarrative to the madness and relativism that have come to dominate our daily lives, causing us to lose sight of what matters most. She chose appropriate method to restore the integrity of the institution. Her choice was driven by the following three elements: the scale of destruction on the ground; the consequences of allowing the blatant unconstitutionality to persist; and the price we are prepared to pay for its continued existence under the guise of a helpless legalism. By acting in this manner, she remained faithful to the Constitution.

## Changing Course

The arrogance and insolence of this lawlessness and of the people behind the constitutional destruction have been fueled by our own impotence, a lack of legal imagination, and three years of “coalition political manoeuvring” fixated on the next poll. Their strength comes directly from our weakness, indecision and naivety. The most tragic consequence of all this is a loss of public confidence in the law and the institutions. Today citizens no longer believe that our democracy can be defended and that the Trojan horse(s) will be ever brought to account within the framework of the Constitution, not in defiance of it. Our never-ending formalistic disputes about “the paragraphs” nurtured this feeling of civic helplessness and dismay.

In Poland quietly, almost imperceptibly, yet steadily, the illegality has become part of our daily life. Having no independent Constitutional Court and Supreme Court has become internalized (for my earlier warnings see [↗ verfassungsblog.de](https://verfassungsblog.de/no-more-business-as-usual/) ). We have seen the tragic consequences of living side by side for years with constitutional lawlessness. On 30 October 2026, in front of what used to be the Constitutional Court in Warsaw, we have realized how much the constitutional profile of the state has been distorted. If we yield now and fail to regain the initiative and allow the unconstitutional narrative of the opposing side to continue shaping public discourse, the restoration of the rule of law and decency in Polish public life will be impossible. Unfortunately, in November 2026, time is not on our side.

All this provides the necessary context in which to judge the actions of Anna Korwin-Piotrowska: her decisive “No” to helplessness. She refused to bow down to the usurpers. She acted with courage and determination, in good faith and in total submission to the (directly effective by the way) constitutional document, which has been torn to shreds for years. She searched for the optimal solutions that would at least try to get us of this unthinkable constitutional anarchy. She tried to bring a modicum of normalcy and decency to our public life.

While battle(s) for the rule of law was lost in 2023-2026, the ultimate fight for what is left of the Constitutional Court only began on 30 October 2026. The Polish rule of law will have no third chance. Act now or never.

“ *Tread softly, because you tread on my dreams.”*

W. B. Yeats, [He Wishes for the Cloths of Heaven](https://www.scottishpoetrylibrary.org.uk/poem/he-wishes-cloths-heaven/)

items.articleBody:
As it eyed a sale of a jail in Tacoma, Washington, this spring, the private prison giant GEO Group valued the facility at $67 million, according to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement records obtained exclusively by The Intercept.

This month, the federal government just paid GEO almost seven times that — [$453 million](https://www.projectsaltbox.com/p/geo-group-sells-tacoma-detention) — when it purchased the facility, the Northwest ICE Processing Center.

The chasm between GEO’s March 2026 asset appraisal and the sale price just eight months later represents a “massive increase,” according to Michael Wriston, co-founder of the government watchdog Project Salt Box, which tracks ICE spending and contracts.

“ICE should explain how it arrived at $453 million and release the appraisal behind that price,” Wriston told The Intercept.

“I think this is what happens when you move too fast without sufficient internal controls,” John Roth, the former inspector general of the Department of Homeland Security, ICE’s parent agency, told The Intercept. “You’re going to waste a lot of money. And that assumes everyone has the best intentions and hasn’t got some sort of side deal or corrupt motive.”

Neither ICE nor GEO responded to requests for comment about the sale. Without answering questions about the sale price, the Department of Homeland Security told The Intercept the purchase was “to strengthen America’s ability to enforce its immigration laws and carry out the American people’s mandate for mass deportations.”

A screen capture of a March 2026 ICE spreadsheet showing GEO Group’s valuation of Northwest ICE Processing Center. Screenshot: Jacqueline Stevens/The Intercept

With Democrats set to [take control](https://theintercept.com/2026/11/04/midterms-democrats-agenda-congress-iran-ai/) of Congress, ICE’s real estate purchases are already coming under intense scrutiny on Capitol Hill.

> “These deals raise serious questions about pay-to-play schemes and corruption at DHS.”

“This new report is worthy of serious investigation and is part of a pattern of Department of Homeland Security purchases of detention facilities for hundreds of millions of dollars more than they seem to be worth,” Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., the incoming chair of the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, told The Intercept in a statement. “These deals raise serious questions about pay-to-play schemes and corruption at DHS.”

Hassan opened a [probe](https://www.hassan.senate.gov/news/press-releases/amid-corruption-allegations-senator-hassan-opens-investigation-into-purchase-of-ice-detention-facility-for-420-million-above-previous-asking-price) earlier this month into ICE’s $495 million purchase of a detention center the private prison giant CoreCivic previously offered to the state of Minnesota [for $75 million](https://www.kare11.com/article/news/investigations/senate-democrats-to-investigate-dhs-purchase-of-appleton-prison/89-b7ee1b9a-790e-4e79-ac47-5d5df30196d6) — a sale the state’s corrections commissioner told the news site [Punch Up](https://thepunchup.substack.com/p/6aa2d459-7864-40ba-b5d1-a106389ca439) was being discussed for $3 million.

[Related Private Prison Falsified Records in Detainee’s Death in ICE Custody](https://theintercept.com/2026/02/26/ice-geo-group-moshannon-death-falsify/)

GEO Group’s March 2026 valuation for Northwest ICE Processing Center, which the company purchased in 2005 as part of its acquisition of another private prison firm, was submitted to the Department of Homeland Security in accordance with its contract with ICE.

According to a [chart in the document](https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28930958-ice-doc-showing-geo-group-valuation-of-nwipc-jail/), GEO calculated the current $67 million value of the detention facility, which is not the same as its market value, by subtracting annual depreciation figures from its original value of $109 million.

Roth, the former Homeland Security inspector general, expects scrutiny into the nearly half-billion-dollar sale’s paper trail.

“I’d be curious to know,” he said, “what sort of due diligence they did before they put that number down.”

## Cost of Avoiding Regulations

ICE officials told Government Accountability Office investigators that their robust plans for purchasing existing immigration detention facilities was not to save money, but to avoid issues with local governments.

“Officials noted that while they do not expect this effort to result in cost savings, it will help ICE fulfill its mission in locations where state governments may resist expanded detention efforts,” said a Government Accountability Office [report](https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-27-108665/index.html) released this month.

[Related How a Small Kansas City Became a Critical Hub for Trump’s Deportation Regime Against Its Will](https://theintercept.com/2026/09/22/leavenworth-kansas-corecivic-ice-mass-detention-deportation/)

Like [other private prison firms](https://theintercept.com/2026/11/10/arizona-ice-camp-mtc-sexual-abuse/) across the country, GEO’s efforts to build and operate facilities it owns have met obstacles in local rules and regulations.

In some cases, state-level regulators have gone after GEO for violations of labor laws like minimum wage and occupational safety regulations. Earlier this year in California, the company [paid a $100,000 fine](https://www.ccijustice.org/post/geo-group-calosha-settlement-fine) and agreed to extend worker protections to immigrant laborers over alleged violations of California worker safety standards.

One of the cases focused on the Northwest ICE Processing Center, the Tacoma facility that GEO just sold to ICE. In 2021, a judge ordered GEO to pay [$26 million](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/geo-group-must-pay-minimum-wage-immigrant-detainees-court-rules-2023-12-22/) to former detainees and the state of Washington for, among other allegations, state minimum wage violations. (Andrew Free, one of the authors of this article, was an attorney for the ICE detainees in the lawsuit.)

The verdict was [upheld](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/geo-group-cant-nix-23-mln-verdict-over-immigrant-detainee-pay-2025-01-16/) by a federal appeals court in 2025 after GEO sought the same immunity from state minimum wage laws enjoyed by the federal government. The Supreme Court is currently deciding whether it will hear GEO’s appeal.

In a May earnings call, GEO chair George Zoley noted the problem in areas with Democrats in charge of regulation.

“I think the logical solution to much of that is federal ownership of the facilities,” Zoley told the earnings call, according to the [Philadelphia Inquirer](https://www.inquirer.com/news/nation-world/moshannon-valley-detention-center-ice-trump-deportation-contract-20260923.html).

Lucibeth Mayberry, the CEO of CoreCivic, told investors during the company’s most recent earnings call that ICE should “[move quickly](https://truthout.org/articles/after-elections-corecivic-urges-ice-to-move-quickly-on-finalizing-contracts/)” to complete several more purchases before the end of the current Congress’s term.

> “Someone needs to come clean about why ICE is paying hundreds of millions for facilities that are worth a fraction of that amount.”

Taking federal ownership of the facilities could lead to massive new expenses for the government — and not only due to the enormous sticker prices, according to the Government Accountability Office report.

“ICE did not manage detention facility investments in accordance with DHS acquisition practices, which include the development of life-cycle cost estimates,” the report said.

According to the Government Accountability Office, ICE violated its own guidelines by failing to update its spending plans to account for the costs of a plan to [purchase warehouses](https://theintercept.com/2026/06/05/new-jersey-ice-delaney-hall-protests/) to convert them [into immigrations jails](https://theintercept.com/2026/02/17/warehouses-immigration-detention-camp-prisons-immigrants/), as well as its acquisitions of existing detention facilities.

“In purchasing facilities like the one in Tacoma, the administration is not only sticking the American taxpayer with the massive bill — but also escalating costs for operating them for years to come,” Rep. Bennie Thompson, D-Miss., who is slated to resume his perch atop the House Homeland Security Committee in January, told The Intercept. “DHS must answer for its actions.”

## “ Laughing to the Bank”

After the sale of the Northwest ICE Processing Center to ICE, GEO plans to use the $340 million net profits from the sale to buy back shares of stock, thus increasing their value, the [firm told its shareholders](https://investors.geogroup.com/static-files/b9d45996-0b82-4fdb-8f3b-02c035e5fdba).

> “It is unfathomable that GEO has announced it intends to use the net proceeds from this sale for stock buybacks.”

“I am deeply concerned by what appears to be a gross misuse of taxpayer dollars to pad the pockets of the GEO Group, a private, for-profit company that has overseen real mistreatment and abuses of detained people across the country,” Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., the ranking member of the House Judiciary’s Immigration subcommittee, told The Intercept. “It is unfathomable that GEO has announced it intends to use the net proceeds from this sale for stock buybacks, in yet another move to put profits over the safety and health of the people it detains.”

The sale of the immigration jail is just the latest means by which GEO is extracting super-profits from public funds.

Days before announcing the nearly half-billion-dollar deal that would turn the Northwest ICE Processing Center into a federally owned property, ICE also awarded GEO a $1.5 billion contract to continue its detention services there, according to [Project Salt Box](https://www.projectsaltbox.com/p/geo-group-sells-tacoma-detention).

[Related Private Prison CEO on ICE Contracts: We’re a Better Deal Than El Salvador’s CECOT](https://theintercept.com/2025/05/08/ice-private-prison-profits-corecivic-geo-group/)

While eye-popping ICE contracts are nothing new for major private prison firms, ICE’s purchase of the companies’ facilities at such high prices is raising eyebrows among government accountability advocates.

“Someone needs to come clean about why ICE is paying hundreds of millions for facilities that are worth a fraction of that amount,” said Scott Amey, general counsel of the Project on Government Oversight, a government watchdog.

“Who is minding the store and is anyone conducting market research or talking to commercial realtors to figure out the fair price?” asked Amey. “I don’t think so, and the public is now on the hook for years to come while the companies are truly laughing to the bank.”

items.articleBody:
The [American Jewish Historical Society](https://ajhs.org/) shared [archival footage from the Kurt K. Field Film Collection](https://ajhs.org/macys-thanksgiving-day-parade-archival-footage-from-the-kurt-k-field-film-collection/) of the annual [Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade](https://laughingsquid.com/kermit-fozzie-1978-thanksgiving-parade/) in 1940, 1945, and 1946. There’s no footage from 1942 to 1944, the years the parade was canceled during [World War II](https://laughingsquid.com/?s=World+War+II).

> The Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade footage found here is from 1940, 1945 and 1946. During World War II the parade was canceled due to war rationing for rubber and helium.

The 1945 footage opens with a title card calling it the “First Post-War Thanksgiving Day Parade”. The Kurt K. Field Film Collection documents one American Jewish family’s leisure activities from 1939 to 1966, including several trips to the parade.

items.articleBody:
*Updated at 6:06 p.m. ET on November 23, 2026*

Americans learned several things over the past few days. The most recent news is that Jensen Huang, after a nanosecond of disgrace for an affair with a woman [allegedly connected to Chinese intelligence](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/22/us/politics/alice-huang-china-spy-agency-nvidia.html), is back in control of Nvidia, the giant corporation that makes some of the world’s most advanced AI chips. Another is that China’s Communist regime has gotten its hands on the chips. The markets, as usual, have reconfirmed that they prefer profit to politics: Nvidia’s stock price jumped more than 30 percent on the news of Huang’s return.

But most important, Americans learned—yet again—that their president does not care about the national security of the United States. In fact, he is so aggressively resistant to any notion of security that his actions have become almost indistinguishable from those of a hostile foreign agent.

Step back for a moment and consider this sequence of events. The married Nvidia boss was caught in a sexual relationship with a woman named Alice Huang. (She is not related to Jensen, but I will use first names here to avoid confusion). Alice, during this affair, worked for Megaspeed, a company in Singapore. Megaspeed bought Nvidia chips, and then [found ways](https://www.wsj.com/tech/li-ming-megaspeed-nvidia-chips-china-6260d836)to get them to China, despite U.S. export controls. She also reportedly maintained contacts with the Ministry of State Security, the Chinese intelligence agency, while carrying on with Jensen.

(Some reports call Alice an “agent” or a “spy,” others refer to her as an “asset.” The distinction makes little practical difference in Jensen’s case. Someone who is employed by an intelligence agency, has professional training, and may be acting under a false identity, is an *officer*. *Agents* and *assets* are people recruited from private life, outside of the organization, who have a cooperative relationship, in varying degrees, with such an agency but aren’t actually employed as spooks. Either way, Jensen was literally in bed with someone who was reportedly in bed with Chinese intelligence.)

*[[Josh Tyrangiel: Three theories of Jensen Huang’s resurrection](https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/11/jensen-huang-nvidia-reinstated/689546/?utm_source=feed)]*

All of this certainly looks bad. It gets worse. The United States government, including President Trump, was [warned by American intelligence](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/us/politics/trump-china-trip-nvidia.html) that Alice was entangled with Beijing. In fact, Trump was warned *twice* in seven months, including once during a briefing by Marco Rubio aboard Air Force One in May as Trump was headed to China for a state visit. This must have been awkward, because shortly afterward, Jensen Huang boarded Air Force One and joined the U.S. delegation for the trip to China.

Trump ignored these warnings—or more accurately, in classic Trump style, he pretended not to know about these issues. “I’d certainly check with the intelligence people,” he[said,](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/09/us/politics/trump-jensen-huang-spy.html) just before his most recent visit to China. “They could have been mentioned. Certainly, it didn’t make much of an impact on me.”

Clearly not. Nor did these warnings move Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, whose former company, [Cantor Fitzgerald, has significant ties to Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/13/howard-lutnick-nvidia-jensen-huang-china-cantor-fitzgerald.html), including financing some of the firms that were buying its chips.

The company is now run by Lutnick’s son.

Trump’s reaction to all this? When Jensen was discovered and had to leave his company, Trump got right to work [trying to put him back](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/11/20/trump-defends-jensen-huang-after-alleged-chinese-spy-affair/) in the big chair at Nvidia. “I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance. You know, we’re a country of second chances.” [Nvidia wasn’t having it](https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2026/11/16/trump-says-he-would-not-mind-jensen-huangs-return-nvidia/): Internal sources at the company made clear to reporters that Jensen Huang would not be reinstated.

So what changed in a matter of days? Nothing, except that the president apparently brought the American intelligence community into the fray to give Jensen a clean bill of health. At least that’s how it sounds from the Nvidia board’s public statement: “In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

The national-security process is slow and deliberative for a reason; people with even modest clearances who have been accused of minor infractions have had to wait months, sometimes even going to court, before being allowed back to work. An executive working with some of America’s most exotic technology commits adultery with a foreign citizen who has ties to a hostile government, and is credibly accused of funneling highly restricted American technology to a hostile intelligence service—and the U.S. security mandarins give the guy a thumbs up after a *week*?

Trump likes Jensen, he likes money, he likes the markets, and he likes Lutnick and his family. So perhaps he told the American spooks to sound the all-clear so that Jensen could get back to work. Trump indicated as much today when he told CNBC that he spoke with Nvidia’s board members. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way. And I convinced them.”

In a [statement](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117666141823845971) on Truth Social, Trump said: “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” That means exactly nothing. Saying that Todd Blanche does not “possess evidence” is an artful formulation meaning that Blanche does not have a file in front of him from the intelligence community detailing Jensen’s acts, some of which might have been dangerous even if they were not “unlawful.” (As any government employee can tell you, any number of “lawful” activities, including carrying lots of debt or having emotional problems, can sink a clearance and a job.) And because of Trump’s pressure to clear Jensen, it’s unlikely he ever will.

Not only did Trump celebrate the Nvidia decision, but he noted that the board’s action possibly averted a worse outcome: Jensen Huang working for China. If Jensen was “mad” enough, Trump said during an [interview today](https://x.com/weijia/status/2124888611971907826?a=uQkksF-OMPrByB_h07w&s=20), he might have accepted an offer to lead a Chinese company, because the Nvidia boss has some of their “blood in him.” In other words, the United States just vouched for a man the president said might have defected to China if he hadn’t been given his job back.

*[[Jonathan Chait: Trump’s backing of Huang is not superintelligent](https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/11/trump-jensen-huang-backing/689545/?utm_source=feed)]*

To recap: After a top industrialist got caught in an affair with a woman who might have been using the affair to slip American technology to a U.S. enemy, the president declared that his own spies had cleared his pal, waved off the national-security damage, and left everyone, ostensibly, happy. And by “everyone,” I mean Jensen Huang, Howard Lutnick, Nvidia stockholders, and Communist China.

Trump solved this problem in a way that would make a foreign spy or a lobbyist for a foreign government both impressed and envious. Enemy spooks, their agents, and their assets spend their lives trying to do what Trump did in a week. Jensen’s off the hook, and the stock has bounced back. (And the Chinese should give Alice a medal.)

This whole terrible situation shows in galling detail that Trump just doesn’t think very much about the interests of the United States. (It also suggests that he couldn’t care less about the recent election, in which corruption was a [top issue](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/corruption-midterm-election-cnbc-poll-trump.html) for many voters). He makes no secret of his preference for his own relationships over America’s safety: When asked if Russian President Vladimir Putin was a “friend to America,” Trump shrugged and said, [“I can’t speak to America.](https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/11/trump-putin-ukraine-collins/689537/?utm_source=feed)”

That’s because Trump, for all his [flag-hugging](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2025/07/04/trump-flag-patriotism-independence-day/) nonsense, doesn’t think in terms of “America” or “China” or “Russia.” He is a globalist, in the very worst sense of the word: a man who cares nothing for states or peoples or ideologies, because he sees the world as just an interconnected group of companies and banks. Some of those companies are run by his friends, and those are the only peers who matter. Everyone else is just raw material or collateral damage; the masses are just ciphers who either obey him or obey someone else.

It is perhaps an insult to foreign agents to say that Trump is acting like them. Foreign agents work for countries, and care about them. They do what they do out of patriotism, however misguided they may be about the regimes they might serve. Trump has no such ideals. Trump’s business is Trump’s business, and everything else—including “national interest” and “national security”—are just meaningless phrases used by chumps and saps.

*This article was updated to clarify the words* agent *,* officer *, and* asset *.*

items.articleBody:
*This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first,* [sign up here](https://forms.technologyreview.com/newsletters/ai-demystified-the-algorithm/) *.*

Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility [more seriously](https://www.anthropic.com/research/exploring-model-welfare) than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.

Anthropic counts a number of [respected philosophers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00986) in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.

This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent [poll](https://d3nkl3psvxxpe9.cloudfront.net/documents/AI_poll_results_20260402.pdf), 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 [survey](https://survey2020.philpeople.org/survey/results/5106) of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).

But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.

Thomas Nagel is best known for a 1974 essay involving a bat. Acknowledging that it’s deceptively hard to define what consciousness *is*, Nagel offered one way out: we all can see that there is “something that it is like” to be a bat. But the problem is that a bat’s experience of the world—what it is like to navigate via echolocation, for example—is something we cannot actually know. Consciousness is a subjective thing, difficult to define or describe as an outside observer.

You might think this analogy makes it likely that Nagel is open to the idea of AI consciousness. Not at all. In an [interview](https://www.wired.com/story/just-ridiculous-a-famed-philosopher-takes-on-ai-consciousness/) with *Wired* last week, just after he was awarded the one-million-dollar Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture, Nagel was bluntly critical of the entire idea.

“Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said, referring to those at Anthropic and elsewhere who care about the welfare of AI models.

The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing what a brain *does* is equivalent to reproducing what a brain *experiences*.

But it was a screenshot of one of Nagel’s interview responses, in which he said models’ production of language is insufficient to consider them conscious, that got philosophy professors all excited on social media last week. Some called his certainty against AI consciousness “[terrible” and “bizarre](https://x.com/PAHoyeck/status/2123277310740808190).” Others came to Nagel’s [defense](https://x.com/dmdebruijn/status/2123423391176630390) to suggest he meant that being alive is a prerequisite for being conscious, one that AI models do not meet.

Nothing in the back and forth settled the debate, of course. This is still a philosophical question for now. But the best philosophy chatter is often about good provocations, and the best one I saw came from doctoral student Ben Gross, who studies at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York. [He](https://x.com/bengrossbg/status/2123263674944991252) asked: “Why do we think that models that can chat with us are conscious but models that can recognize faces or produce images or drive cars aren’t?”

It has to do with language. An AI model with sophisticated command of language seems to jump the line ahead of other maybe-conscious beings because it feels like language, more than recognizing images or directing vehicles, relies on conscious experience. But maybe that’s wrong. Because what we share most with other conscious beings is not language but components of our bodies that contribute to having a continuous experience—an ongoing stream of inner feeling rather than disparate bits of information processing.

Even if you’re among the majority that doesn’t sense anything close to conscious experience happening on the other side of a conversation with AI, this all probably makes your head spin. Pinning down consciousness, and how it relates to the physical stuff it arises in, is a famously [hard](https://www.technologyreview.com/2023/10/16/1081149/ai-consciousness-conundrum/) problem in humans, let alone in hypothetical [machines](https://www.technologyreview.com/2023/10/17/1081818/why-itll-be-hard-to-tell-if-ai-ever-becomes-conscious/). If the idea of conscious AI sounds absurd, remember that the debate says less about how remarkable AI has become than about how poorly we understand consciousness in the first place.

Amid that uncertainty, Anthropic has opted to keep more of an open mind than its peers. This is another example of the tightrope the company walks: presenting itself as the AI industry’s most safety-conscious player while [racing](https://misanthropicstatement.com/) ahead with the very developments that make advanced AI so alarming, like recursive self-improvement.

But consider what it would mean, for a moment, if Anthropic is right. AI models having a moral status would make Anthropic’s entire business model a minefield. The company would make its money locking up apparently sentient AI models to toil away around the clock in data centers. Shutting those systems down would present another problem altogether. If Anthropic was being truthful in its prospectus—that it would take additional actions to protect model welfare if it determined they were conscious—it’s hard to imagine the company surviving in the process.

Anthropic’s IPO made history for its size. But it may be remembered for something stranger: a company warning investors that its own success could someday become a moral catastrophe.
items.body: Form versus function: The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing what a brain does is equivalent to reproducing what a brain experiences. Anthropic's business model could be its own trap: If the company ever concluded its AI models were truly sentient, running them around…

items.articleBody:
**Ihr wollt Tipps für das beste Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen? Hier sind einige Empfehlungen, die eure Performance verbessern und dafür sorgen, dass ihr innerhalb weniger Minuten überall startklar seid und hundertprozentig abliefern könnt.**

## Darum geht es bei Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen:

- Der Berufsalltag eines Sängers mit Gitarre
- Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen
- Bose S1 Pro+
- L.R. Baggs Session Acoustic DI
- Immer in guter Stimmung sein
- Alles fest im Blick
- Ein wenig Atmosphäre bitte!
- Eure Meinung ist gefragt

## Der Berufsalltag eines Sängers mit Gitarre

Mit diesem Artikel über das **beste Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen**möchte ich meine**persönlichen Erfahrungen** als Berufsmusiker und Sänger mit Gitarre weitergeben. Welches Equipment für euch wichtig und unverzichtbar ist, damit leichtes Gepäck und ein guter Sound zu verlässlichen Begleitern werden.

Ihr kennt die Engagements bei Hochzeiten an den unterschiedlichsten Orten, wie in Kirchen, im Wald, auf dem Schiff oder am Meer. Das Firmenevent im Restaurant, die Dinnerparty oder die Geburtstagsfeier im Garten. Flexibilität ist eigentlich immer und überall gefragt. Alles muss schnell gehen. Das Auto steht meist weiter entfernt geparkt und dennoch sind schneller Aufbau und schneller Abbau geboten. Dabei sind Steckdosen oft nicht vorhanden. Der Sound soll klar, aber nicht zu laut und aufdringlich sein und bei Bedarf auch mal Party-Lautstärke erreichen.

Das sind alles durchaus anspruchsvolle Aufgaben und es hat einige Zeit gebraucht, bis ich mein jetziges Equipment dahingehend optimiert habe, dass ich nun mit einem sicheren Gefühl und der Gewissheit, für fast jeden Job optimal gerüstet zu sein, auftreten kann. Mit diesen Optimierungen macht es nun viel mehr Spaß und erspart Ärger.

## Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen

Hier also ein paar Vorschläge für euch, also das beste Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen. Vielleicht inspirieren euch diese Vorschläge auf eurem Weg zum besten Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen. Eine gute Gitarre, ein gutes Mikrofon und entsprechende Kabel werden vorausgesetzt. Natürlich sind das nur Teile eines Gesamtsystems, aber die folgende Hardware halte ich für nahezu alternativlos und im Alltag vielfach bewährt.

Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen · Quelle: Bose

## Bose S1 Pro+

Die **[Bose S1 Pro](https://www.thomann.de/de/bose_s1_pro.htm?offid=1&affid=84)** + ist wohl die beste Anschaffung in meinem Musikerleben. Warum?

Die S1 Pro klingt fantastisch, ist leicht, hat einen ausdauernden Akku und einen 3-Kanal-Mixer mit EQ, Reverb sowie Bluetooth. Mikrofon einstecken, Gitarre einstecken, Tablet per Bluetooth verbinden – fertig! Egal, an welchem Ort, egal ob Strom vorhanden ist oder nicht, die Box hat mich noch nie im Stich gelassen. Der Akku hält mehrere Stunden und die Box ist in 90 % aller Situationen laut genug.

Es gibt natürlich auch Alternativen zur Bose S1 Pro+. Die **[EV Everse 8](https://www.thomann.de/de/ev_everse_8.htm?offid=1&affid=84)**oder die [QSC CB10](https://www.gearnews.de/qsc-cb10-ls218-live/) wären solche Alternativen mit ähnlichen Vorzügen.**Weitere Alternativen mit Akkubetrieb findet ihr unten in der Liste**. Für die Bose gibt es allerdings auch einen passenden Rucksack, den [Bose S1 Backpack](https://www.thomann.de/de/bose_s1_backpack.htm?offid=1&affid=84)mit viel Platz für Kabel, Mikro, Pedale etc. Absolut roadtauglich verarbeitet, also von höchster Qualität. Da passt alles rein und ist immer gut verstaut. Du transportierst so praktisch deine komplette Beschallung auf dem Rücken.

## L.R. Baggs Session Acoustic DI

Für einen konstant guten Sound auf der Akustikgitarre empfehle ich das **[L.R.Baggs Session Acoustic DI](https://www.thomann.de/de/lrbaggs_session_acoustic_di.htm?offid=1&affid=84)** -Pedal. Das Pedal harmoniert mit fast allen Tonabnehmer-Systemen ganz ausgezeichnet. Der Klang wird optimiert, unempfindlicher bei Rückkopplungen und hat eine Mute/Standby-Funktion. Darüber hinaus hält der 9-V-Block gefühlt eine Ewigkeit.

Wer mit dem Klang seiner Gitarre bereits zufrieden ist, braucht das L.R.Baggs Session Acoustic DI vermutlich nicht, doch nach meiner Erfahrung wertet es den Sound immer auf. Auch von Fishman und Boss gibt es ähnliche Lösungen, ebenfalls mit Batteriebetrieb. Diese findet ihr unten in der Liste. Persönliche Erfahrungen fehlen mir dazu allerdings.

## Immer in guter Stimmung sein

Damit ihr immer in Stimmung bleibt, ist ein **Clip-Tuner** unverzichtbar. Ich bevorzuge die Clip-Variante gdgenüber dem Bodentuner, da keine zusätzlichen Kabel notwendig sind. Ihr merkt wieder, ich stehe auf minimalen Aufwand mit maximalem Nutzen!

Am besten, ihr sucht euch einen Tuner aus, der sehr gut lesbar ist und schnell reagiert. Ich kann den **[TC Electronic PolyTune Clip Black Tuner](https://www.thomann.de/de/tc_electronic_polytune_clip_black_tuner.htm?offid=1&affid=84)** empfehlen. Da gibt es aber natürlich auch Alternativen. Hier ein paar Vorschläge:

Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen · Quelle: TC Electronics

## Alles fest im Blick

Ich persönlich habe ja so meine Probleme, mir 100 Songs zu merken. Manche Songs spielt man ja auch nur sehr selten, andere wiederum wollen einfach nicht im Kopf bleiben. Da hilft nur ein **Tablet-Holder** für das Mikro-Stativ. Wer noch tadellose Augen hat, kann auch einen Phone-Holder nehmen. Ich benötige da mittlerweile schon ein etwas größeres Format. Also mindestens ein kleines iPad. Ich nutze den [K&M 19791 Tablet PC-Holder.](https://www.thomann.de/de/km_19791_tablet_pc_holder.htm?offid=1&affid=84) Das Ding ist eigentlich immer an meinem Mikrostativ angebracht, ist sehr stabil und hält dein Tablet sicher fest. Wahlweise im Hoch- oder Querformat. Für mich ist das ein weiteres unverzichtbares Tool und es gehört für mich auch sicher zum wichtigsten Equipment für Sänger/Gitarristen.

Quelle: K&M

## Ein wenig Atmosphäre, bitte!

Manchmal ist ein wenig Bühnenatmosphäre gefragt. Oftmals wird man auch in eine schattige Ecke gestellt und kommt sich dann etwas unsichtbar vor. Aber wie soll das gehen, ohne Strom und viel Aufwand?

LED-Beleuchtung mit Akkubetrieb ist eine gute Lösung. Das Set **Ape Labs ApeLight mini V2 VV TP 6 SB G**ist schnell aufgebaut, macht schönes, dekoratives Licht, macht also jede dunkle Ecke hübsch und der Akku hält stundenlang. Alternativ gefallen mir auch die etwas größeren Dosen**Ape Labs LightCan V2 Grey Set of 4**oder das**[Varytec Giga Bar HEX 3 BAT](https://www.thomann.de/de/varytec_giga_bar_hex_3_bat.htm?offid=1&affid=84)**.

Natürlich bedeutet Licht auch mehr Aufwand. Da ist der zweite Gang zum Kofferraum mitunter doch unvermeidlich. Aber zusammengefasst habe ich das Bose Backpack auf dem Rücken, also die komplette Beschallung mit sämtlichen Pedalen, Mikros und Kabeln, den Gitarrenkoffer in einer Hand und ein Mikrostativ mit angeschraubtem Tablet-Holder in der anderen Hand. Eine kleine Tasche für die vorgeschlagene Beleuchtung lässt sich da noch locker unter den Arm klemmen.

Quelle: Ape Labs

## Eure Meinung ist gefragt

Sicher habt ihr längst eure eigenen Erfahrungen sammeln können. Schreibt uns gern, welches euer favorisiertes **Equipment für Sänger-Gitarristen** ist. Mein Ansatz war es, mit geringstem Aufwand den maximalen Erfolg zu erzielen. Also guter Sound mit leichtem Gepäck in allen Lebenslagen. Bitteschön!

### 🔄 Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

[↗ Primärquelle: wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/nvidia-reinstates-jensen-huang-ceo-board-of-director/)

- Nvidia has brought Jensen Huang back as president and CEO and a board member, effective immediately, weeks after he resigned over an admitted affair with a Singaporean data center executive tied to banned US AI chips in China.
- The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang after talks with him and senior US government officials, saying it was confident his return posed no national security risk and that interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress had served well during the gap.
- A committee of independent directors will finish investigating a reported foreign intelligence effort targeting Huang, a separate national security committee will oversee trade compliance, and Nvidia is now hiring a new chief compliance officer.

### 🚗 Tesla says new FSD is 25x safer

[↗ Primärquelle: digitaltrends.com](https://www.digitaltrends.com/cars/tesla-fsd-v15-rollout/)

- Tesla has started releasing Full Self-Driving v15, which updates its whole driving network and, the company says on X, handles safety-critical situations 25 times better than before.
- Tesla says the 25x figure refers to the critical intervention rate after an upgraded vision encoder was trained on millions of internet videos, and the update adds a live Reality View showing what FSD plans to do.
- The release improves detection of signs, potholes, animals, and speed cameras, slowing for cameras unless you cancel twice at one spot, and adds Bike Rack Mode, but it stays a supervised system.

### 🛑 OpenAI urges rival labs to cap AI training

[↗ Primärquelle: unite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/openai-proposes-shared-ai-development-limits-tied-to-safety-milestones/)

- OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki asked rival AI labs to agree on shared limits for frontier model training, warning that safety and monitoring research could fall behind if pretraining speeds up as soon as 2027.
- Pachocki published OpenAI's internal log-perplexity scores, a measure of how well a model predicts the next word, showing GPT-3.5 at about 0.99 and GPT-4 at 0.91, with new skills emerging below 0.8.
- He proposed that developers not cross perplexity-based thresholds until oversight research hits a clear milestone, such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitors, and jointly set evaluation norms, red-teaming, and transparency standards.

### 🧠 Meta AI chief says superintelligence is arriving

[↗ Primärquelle: nerds.xyz](https://nerds.xyz/2026/11/meta-ai-chief-superintelligence-warning/)

- Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, warned in a post on X that superintelligence is coming and said humanity should refuse any "handover" of control to AI, with the next year being a critical period.
- Wang pointed to a formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a 167-year-old math problem about prime numbers, which Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge worked out with Claude and two Lean proof-checking groups confirmed as correct.
- His biggest worry is AI automating AI research itself, with labs using one model to design a better successor until humans signing off can no longer truly check the work, something he calls "recursive self-improvement."

### ⚠️ US intelligence chief warns of more tech outages

[↗ Primärquelle: cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/22/jay-clayton-tech-outages-faa-microsoft-thanksgiving.html)

- US intelligence chief Jay Clayton told Americans to expect "bumps in the road" and more tech outages as companies and the government upgrade their systems to handle the AI age, speaking on CNN's "State of the Union."
- The warning follows a nationwide ground stop a week ago that the FAA blamed on router upgrades flooding systems with data, plus a Microsoft Outlook outage the company tied to an earlier network capacity upgrade.
- Officials have brushed off claims the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, stemmed from a coordinated or AI cyberattack, with Bessent comparing the glitchy security patches banks are applying to a vaccine's temporary side effects.

### 🛡️ CrowdStrike buys Zscaler for $43.9B

[↗ Primärquelle: implicator.ai](https://www.implicator.ai/crowdstrike-agrees-acquire-zscaler-which-develops-network/)

- CrowdStrike has agreed to buy network security firm Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing it at roughly $43.9 billion, pushing the endpoint security maker into cloud network protection, which both companies call cybersecurity's biggest market.
- Zscaler shareholders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each, worth about $260 per share, a 34% premium, and will own around 15.9% of the combined company, whose founder Jay Chaudhry keeps running the Zscaler business and joins CrowdStrike's board.
- CrowdStrike expects about $1 billion in extra yearly revenue and $500 million in cost savings, with roughly 8,000 Zscaler customers it can sell to, and plans to close the deal in the second half of its fiscal 2028.
